title: incident-bot: oncall autodiagnostics enhancements and SLO toolkit helpers
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: During recent on-call rotations and a P1 incident we observed that the incident-bot autodiagnostics often surfaced noisy or irrelevant runbook links and lacked SLO-aware prioritization for suggested diagnostics. This PR improves autodiagnostics relevance by adding SLO-toolkit heuristics, on-call helper endpoints, and richer telemetry for ranking suggestions. Summary of changes: 1) SLO toolkit helpers: add a new set of utilities (slo_toolkit/helpers.py) that compute SLO impact scores for incidents based on recent burn rate, error budget, and customer tier. These helpers are intentionally lightweight and have unit tests; 2) Autodiagnostics ranking: incident-bot core now calls the SLO impact heuristics when generating runbook suggestions and ranks suggestions by combined score (relevance + SLO impact); 3) On-call helper endpoints: added two new HTTP endpoints to the oncall service to retrieve prioritized runbook suggestions and a compact runbook summary for quick Slack attachments; 4) Telemetry: augment incident-bot diagnostics pipeline to emit ranking metadata (score components, decision reason) to tracing/metrics so we can iterate on ranking models; 5) Tests and CI: end-to-end integration test that exercises the autodiagnostics flow with synthetic SLO signals; update unit tests and mock fixtures. Backwards compatibility: default behavior remains unchanged when SLO signals are missing (the heuristics are a no-op). Rollout plan: feature gated behind feature flag "autodiag_slo_ranking" (off by default for prod) and can be enabled per-org. Related: ENG-4321, ENG-4378, PR #212345 (runbook canonicalization).
commits: Integrate slo heuristics into autodiag ranking
Expose oncall endpoints for prioritized suggestions
Emit ranking metadata to telemetry pipeline
Add integration test for autodiag with synthetic SLO signals
